(5) Add constraint templates — predefined buttons for common constraints ('No new content', 'Focus on testing', 'Budget cap 10 heats').

Constraint Board improvements (batch 2). In ui-constraint-board/: (1) Add visual constraint categories — group cards by type (budget, progress, block, deadline, custom) with section headers. (2) Add constraint impact preview — when hovering a constraint, show what would change in the allocator (which stages would be blocked/boosted). (3) Add 'active constraints' count in page title/header. (4) Add edit-in-place for constraint values (click the number to change it). (5) Add history log — show when each constraint was added/removed/triggered.

Constraint Board improvements (batch 3). In ui-constraint-board/: (1) Add smart constraint suggestions — based on current state, suggest constraints that might be useful ('research is at 90%, consider capping it'). Read state.json stages and propose. (2) Add constraint conflicts detection — warn if two constraints are contradictory ('block testing' + 'testing must stay above 80%'). (3) Add a 'what if' mode — temporarily add a constraint and see the simulated allocator output without persisting. Call smithy allocate with modified state. (4) Add keyboard shortcut 'n' to open new constraint form.

Timeline improvements (batch 1). In ui-timeline/: (1) After t-205 wires up drag, add snap-to-grid — snap to 5-heat increments on drag. (2) Add conflict detection — when total allocated heats exceed remaining budget, show a red warning bar and color overflowing bars red. (3) Add zoom controls — buttons for 50/100/250 heat view range, resize the timeline canvas accordingly. (4) Add initiative labels on bars with text truncation (ellipsis if too long). (5) Add 'now' marker — a vertical dashed line at current heat count with label.

Timeline improvements (batch 2). In ui-timeline/: (1) Add tooltip on hover — show initiative title, description, task count, heats_used/budget_cap, theme name. (2) Add auto-refresh — poll state.json every 5s, update bar fills to show Forge progress in real-time. (3) Add color coding — use theme colors or stage colors for bars. (4) Add summary row at bottom showing total allocated vs remaining heats. (5) Add new initiative creation — click empty space on timeline to create a bar, opens a form for title/description/theme.

Timeline improvements (batch 3). In ui-timeline/: (1) Add bar stacking — when bars overlap, stack them vertically with a subtle offset so both are visible. (2) Add dependency arrows — if one initiative blocks another (via task blocked_by), draw an arrow between them. (3) Add a compact 'plan' view that shows just bars without the y-axis labels. (4) Add undo for drag operations — store previous state client-side, show undo bar for 5s after any change. (5) Add keyboard navigation — left/right to select bars, shift+arrows to resize.

Intent Editor improvements (batch 1). In ui-intent-editor/: (1) Show current state.json themes/initiatives in the right panel on page load (not just after Apply). Read from GET /api/state endpoint. (2) Add Claude API integration for decomposition — when human submits intent, POST to /decompose endpoint that calls Claude (claude-sonnet-4-6 via anthropic SDK) with prompt: 'Given this intent and current project state, decompose into themes and initiatives. Return JSON matching state.json schema.' Show the proposed decomposition as a tree. (3) Add diff view — highlight what's new vs what already exists in state.json. Green = new, yellow = modified. (4) Selective apply — checkboxes on each node in the decomposition tree, Apply only creates checked items.

Intent Editor improvements (batch 2). In ui-intent-editor/: (1) Add intent history — store previous intents with timestamps in state.json or intents.json, show in a sidebar. Click to reload a previous intent. (2) Add 'current state' diff indicator — show how active state.json differs from what the last intent produced (initiatives added/removed outside the editor). (3) Add task preview — when hovering an initiative in the tree, show proposed tasks that would be generated. (4) Add natural language constraint extraction — if the intent says 'no more than 10 heats on research', auto-create a constraint card (integrate with constraint board data model).

Intent Editor improvements (batch 3). In ui-intent-editor/: (1) Add iterative refinement — human edits intent, resubmits, sees diff of what changed vs previous decomposition. Only changed items highlighted. (2) Add template intents — predefined buttons for common intents ('Focus on testing and polish', 'Build new feature: [name]', 'Research and prototype'). (3) Add split view — left panel shows raw intent text, right panel shows structured tree, both scrollable and linked. (4) Add export — button to copy the current decomposition as CLI commands (smithy add-theme, smithy propose) for use outside the editor.
Plan 60-heat sprint: UI polish + constraint enforcement + tutor content + testing

UI reactivity: manual refresh on all 4 UIs. For each of ui-priority-poker/, ui-constraint-board/, ui-timeline/, ui-intent-editor/: (1) Add GET /api/state endpoint in app.py that returns the current UI-relevant data as JSON (initiatives, themes, tasks, constraints — whatever that UI displays). (2) Add a visible 'Refresh' button in the page header (top-right, subtle but always visible). (3) Add JS function refreshState() that fetches /api/state and re-renders the DOM without full page reload — update card contents, progress bars, counts, violation status etc. (4) Wire the Refresh button to call refreshState(). (5) Show a brief 'Updated' flash indicator after successful refresh. Use the same dark theme button styling. Priority Poker already has some AJAX — extend its pattern to the other 3.

UI reactivity: SSE enhancement. For each of the 4 UIs: (1) Add GET /events SSE endpoint in app.py that watches state.json for modification (use os.path.getmtime polling at 2s interval in an async generator — simpler than watchdog). Yield a 'state-changed' event when mtime changes. (2) Add JS EventSource connection to /events. On 'state-changed' event, call refreshState() automatically. (3) Show a subtle 'live' indicator dot in the header when SSE is connected (green = connected, gray = disconnected). (4) Fallback: if SSE disconnects, the manual Refresh button still works. No auto-polling — SSE is event-driven.

initiatives.title: Logic Subject Expansion
initiatives.description: Add more topics and exercises to Logic & Critical Thinking

initiatives.title: Collaboration patterns landscape
initiatives.description: Research how humans and AI agents collaborate effectively. Survey existing frameworks: OODA loops, PDCA, delegation matrices, trust calibration, oversight gradients (from full autonomy to pair programming). Study real systems: Devin, Cursor, Codex, aider, Claude Code, GPT-Pilot. Identify patterns that Smithy doesn't use yet. Deliverable: research/collaboration-patterns.md with a taxonomy of collaboration modes and recommendations for which to prototype.

initiatives.title: Async handoff protocols
initiatives.description: Research and design better async handoff between human and AI. Current model: inbox.md/outbox.md + dispatch files. Problems: context loss between sessions, no structured status requests, human has to read raw files. Explore: structured status requests (human asks a question, gets an answer next heat), decision queues with deadlines, progress summaries that compress intelligently, proactive alerts (not just outbox dumps). Deliverable: research doc + design for improved async protocol.

initiatives.title: Trust and autonomy calibration
initiatives.description: Research how to dynamically adjust AI autonomy based on track record. Currently Forge has fixed autonomy (full within budget). Explore: earned autonomy (start supervised, earn independence), risk-based gating (low-risk tasks auto-approved, high-risk need human), confidence signals (AI reports its own uncertainty, human decides when to intervene), learning from corrections (human corrects, AI adjusts future behavior). Deliverable: research doc + design for adaptive autonomy.

initiatives.title: Terminal dashboard (Rich)
initiatives.description: Build a terminal-based dashboard using Python Rich library. Real-time view of Forge state without leaving the terminal. Shows: budget bar, stage progress (colored bars), current heat, last 5 worklog entries, pending tasks, initiative board (compact). Single command: 'smithy dashboard' that refreshes on file changes (watchdog or polling). Complements Bellows — Bellows for steering, terminal for monitoring while Forge runs.

initiatives.title: Slack/Discord bot interface
initiatives.description: Build a bot that bridges Forge to a messaging platform. Human sends messages in Slack/Discord, they appear in inbox.md. Forge outbox updates post to a channel. Decision cards become interactive messages with approve/defer/reject buttons. Status requests return formatted summaries. Start with one platform (likely Discord — free, good bot API). Lightweight: just a bridge, not a replacement for Bellows.

initiatives.title: Email digest
initiatives.description: Build an email digest that summarizes Forge activity. Daily or per-run summary sent via email (or written to a file for manual sending). Contains: heats completed, stage progress deltas, decisions needing attention, notable events (yellows/reds), link to Bellows. Template-based (Jinja2). Could also serve as the foundation for a webhook/notification system.

initiatives.title: Mobile-first Bellows redesign
initiatives.description: Redesign Bellows for phone-first use. Current Bellows is desktop-oriented. The human checks status from their phone more than laptop. Key screens: (1) project list with signal dots — one glance, (2) initiative approval — swipe to approve/reject, (3) status summary — compact, no scrolling needed. CSS-only responsive or a separate mobile template. PWA with push notifications for decisions.

initiatives.title: Steering patterns research
initiatives.description: Research how humans steer autonomous systems — not monitor, STEER. The core question: what controls does a human need to change direction without becoming a bottleneck? Study: (1) Real-time strategy games (StarCraft command hierarchy — strategic goals, tactical orders, unit autonomy), (2) Military C2 frameworks (mission-type orders, commander's intent, OODA), (3) Product management (OKRs, roadmap prioritization, sprint planning), (4) Air traffic control (constraints not commands), (5) Existing AI tools (Devin's chat-to-steer, Cursor's accept/reject, Claude Code hooks). For each, extract: what decisions the human makes, at what frequency, what information they need to decide, and what the feedback loop looks like. Deliverable: research/steering-patterns.md with a taxonomy of steering modes and which are worth prototyping as UIs.

initiatives.title: UI A: Priority poker
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by ranking, not approving. Shows all active initiatives as cards. Human drags to reorder — that IS the steering. No approve/reject buttons. Everything proposed is fair game unless explicitly killed. The ranking determines allocation weight. Top card gets 3x budget share, second gets 2x, rest get 1x. Real-time: as Forge works, cards show live progress and the stack rebalances. The human's only job: keep the stack in the right order. Inspired by planning poker + priority queues. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: UI B: Constraint board
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by setting constraints, not giving orders. Instead of telling Forge what to do, the human defines boundaries: 'no more than 5 heats on research', 'testing must stay above 80%', 'don't touch tutor', 'ship something deployable by Friday'. Constraints are cards on a board. Forge works freely within them. When a constraint would be violated, Forge stops and asks. The human's only job: add/remove/adjust constraints. Inspired by air traffic control — direct through boundaries, not waypoints. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: UI C: Timeline view
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by shaping a timeline. Horizontal axis is heats (or time). Initiatives are horizontal bars showing planned start/end. The human drags bar endpoints to allocate budget. Overlapping bars = parallel work. Gaps = cool-down. The visual makes tradeoffs obvious — stretching one initiative squeezes another. Forge reads the timeline and works accordingly. Inspired by Gantt charts but interactive and simple. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: UI D: Intent editor
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI focused on natural-language steering. The human writes a short intent statement (2-3 sentences). The system decomposes it into themes, initiatives, and tasks automatically. Human reviews the decomposition and edits — delete a branch, promote a task, add a constraint. The intent is the source of truth, not the task list. When intent changes, the decomposition updates. Inspired by commander's intent in military doctrine. The human thinks in outcomes, the system thinks in tasks. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: UI reactivity — state change detection
initiatives.description: All 4 steering UIs should reflect state.json changes without auto-polling. Options: (1) Manual refresh button visible on every UI — 'Refresh' button in header that reloads data via AJAX (not full page reload). (2) File watcher via SSE — backend watches state.json with watchdog/inotify and pushes events to frontend via Server-Sent Events. Frontend updates DOM on event. (3) Hybrid — manual refresh button always visible, plus optional SSE for live updates. Start with manual refresh button on all 4 UIs (simplest, no dependencies). Then add SSE as an enhancement. Each UI needs: a GET /api/state endpoint returning current data as JSON, a JS function that fetches it and re-renders the relevant DOM elements, a visible Refresh button in the header that calls this function.
